title: Uniform-in-time quantitative empirical-measure convergence for one-dimensional Riesz gases with exponent between one and two, quadratic confinement and vanishing noise
source_title: On systems of particles in singular repulsive interaction in dimension one: log and Riesz gas
author: Arnaud Guillin; Pierre Le Bris; Pierre Monmarché
difficulty_reason: The singular force prevents a direct Lipschitz mean-field coupling even after the standard Ito, BDG and Wasserstein completeness prerequisites are supplied. The authors compare different particle counts by replication and prove a new index-weighted interaction-energy bound that controls the singular discrepancies and yields an explicit algebraic error rate. They then combine the complete uniform-time and path-supremum comparisons with independence of the empirical systems to obtain a deterministic continuous limit, rather than a random subsequential measure.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem4 Riesz branch only: V prime(x)=-x/|x|^(alpha+1), 1<alpha<2, U(x)=lambda*x²/2 with lambda>0, ordered initial particle data and expected squared Wasserstein-two empirical convergence to rho0 in P2(R); diffusion sigmaN>=0 tends to zero. A deterministic continuous family rho_t exists and satisfies the displayed uniform-in-time bound e^(-2lambda*t) C0N + C1 N^(-(2-alpha)/alpha)+C2 sigmaN, with C0N tending to zero. Full new replicated comparison17–25, independence/Cauchy construction26–28 and weighted interaction energy core42–47 read; no-collision/existence10–14 and contraction15 read. The final scalar bound is the bounded routine limiting application of authored Lemma3.2 after Lemmas3.4–3.5, not an assistant-derived replacement proof. Named Ito, BDG, Gronwall and Wasserstein completeness are traced background. No general convex confinement in the Riesz branch, constant-noise limit, alpha>=2, or separate PDE-identification claim.
